Kimberly / Ben / Andrew —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick read / proposed middle ground below — aiming for something procurement can accept while protecting Redwood's exposure. I'll attach a tracked version after this note.

Proposed position (short):
1) Defense vs Reimburse: Redwood will agree to assume defense of covered third‑party IP claims alleging infringement by the Service as delivered ("Covered Claims"), but we request the right to control defense and to select counsel. If Redwood assumes defense and obtains a settlement that releases BrightFarm, Redwood will not seek reimbursement for reasonable defense costs (no double recovery). For claims arising from Customer modifications or content, Customer will be responsible (reimburse).

2) Notice & Cooperation: Claims require prompt written notice (within 30 days of receipt). Failure to provide timely notice that materially prejudices Redwood’s defense could shift liability back to BrightFarm. Cooperation includes evidence transfer and reasonable access to logs/KV cache for triage; we propose a secured evidence staging bucket with documented SLAs for retrieval (48‑72 hours).

3) Evidence & Privilege: To protect privilege, Redwood proposes an "evidence handoff protocol": minimal privileged materials are preserved; technical evidence (logs, call traces) is shared under a narrow scope and NDA. If BrightFarm needs an extended forensic set, we bill at fixed rates or pull from a pre‑approved incident credit.

4) Cap & Insurance offset: Redwood proposes a mutual cap tied to the relevant Order Form (aggregate cap tied to 12x monthly recurring fees for the contract year) and an insurance offset provision (if Redwood's insurer pays, the cap is reduced accordingly). We will not agree to uncapped exposure for routine service use.

5) Limited carveouts: Exclude claims stemming from BrightFarm's integrations or unapproved model fine‑tuning.

Next steps: I will upload a tracked PDF (RW_proposed_redlines.pdf) with inline language and a short comment for each change. Kimberly — if this looks good, propose a 30‑minute bridge with Andrew and procurement on Oct 1 11:00 PT. Ben — please advise whether a one‑time onboarding credit ($X) or a 3‑month SLA credit is easier to approve from finance for deal closure.

Jordan Blake

- Cap level: the 12x MRR anchor is reasonable; procurement will want a numeric example on the order form so finance can run models.

Attached is our PO draft for timeline context (BrightFarm_PO_draft.pdf). Procurement is aligned to finish commercial terms by Oct 15; legal wants the MSA language locked by Oct 8 to allow internal review.
